# PCVX (Vaxcyte, Inc.) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-09 | Verified close: 71.38**

## Executive Summary

PCVX underwent a violent repricing event on 2026-10-05, gapping from a 56.48 close (2026-10-02) to an open of 87.21 — a ~54% overnight gap on 14.9M shares (vs. a typical ~1–2M daily volume). Since then the stock has been in high-volatility price discovery: it faded to 65.01 by 2026-10-08, then rallied +9.8% on 2026-10-09 to close at 71.38, essentially at the verified upper Bollinger band (71.13). All trend indicators are bullishly aligned, but volatility is extreme (ATR 4.88, ~7% of price) and the gap zone remains untested. This is a momentum market, not a mean-reversion market — position sizing matters more than entry precision.

## Price Action & the Gap Event

- Pre-event (July–early Oct): PCVX chopped sideways-to-down in a broad 52.5–63.8 range, deteriorating through September to a local low of 56.05 on 2026-10-01.
- 2026-10-05: open 87.21, high 90.75, low 71.60, close 73.82 on 14.9M shares — a ~7–10x volume surge. The intraday fade from the open shows heavy supply into the spike.
- 2026-10-06 to 10-08: consolidation between ~63.8 and ~67, still on elevated volume (10.2M, 11.6M, 3.8M). The low of the entire post-gap range is ~63.79 (2026-10-08).
- 2026-10-09: strong reversal candle — open 64.78 at the day's low, closed 71.38 near the high of 72.44 on 4.4M shares. Buyers defended the low-64s and reclaimed the 10-05 close region.

Key levels from verified data: resistance at 71.60 (gap-day low) / 72.44 (2026-10-09 high), then 87.21–90.75 (gap-day open/high). Support at ~64.8 (2026-10-09 open/low), ~63.8 (post-gap low), then the gap fill zone toward 56.48.

## Indicator Readings (verified snapshot, 2026-10-09)

- **Trend:** Close 71.38 > 10 EMA 64.43 > 50 SMA 59.94 > 200 SMA 55.73. Full bullish stack — and the 50 SMA is well above the 200 SMA and rising. However, the moving averages are still digesting the gap; the 10 EMA jumped from 57.21 to 64.43 in five sessions.
- **Momentum:** MACD 2.22 vs. signal 0.89, histogram +1.33 — a fresh, strongly positive crossover driven by the gap. RSI 64.88: elevated but below the 70 overbought line; it spiked to 76.6 on 10-05, cooled to ~57–61, and is now re-expanding — consistent with a second momentum leg rather than exhaustion.
- **Volatility:** Bollinger bands have exploded apart (UB 71.13 / LB 50.05, width ~21 pts vs. ~4 pts in mid-Sept). Price closed right at the upper band — in a strong trend prices can ride the band, but it also marks the immediate resistance confluence with 72.44.
- **Risk sizing:** ATR 4.88 (~6.8% of price) vs. ~2.2 pre-gap — more than doubled. Stops and position sizes calibrated to the old regime are now ~2x too tight/large.

## Actionable Insights

- **Bull case:** The 10-09 candle (open = low, close near high) plus rising MACD histogram suggests the post-gap consolidation resolved upward. Holding above ~66–67 keeps the structure constructive; a break above 72.44 opens a retest of 87–90.
- **Bear case / risk:** A close back below ~64 (the post-gap demand zone) weakens the reversal and exposes a partial gap fill toward 56–58. The 10-05 intraday fade from 87 shows trapped supply overhead.
- **Practical:** Use ATR-based stops (~4.9 pts minimum) and halve position size vs. normal-volatility sizing. Momentum entries belong above 72.44; value entries belong near 64–66 with defined risk below 63.8. Chasing mid-range between 68–72 has the worst reward-to-risk.
- RSI is supportive but not a timing edge here; the binding constraints are volatility and the overhead supply shelf from the gap day.

## Key Points Table

| Category | Signal | Evidence (verified) | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trend | Bullish stack | 71.38 > 10EMA 64.43 > 50SMA 59.94 > 200SMA 55.73 | Bullish |
| Momentum | MACD cross up, RSI re-expanding | MACD 2.22 > signal 0.89; RSI 64.88 (< 70) | Bullish, not overbought |
| Event | ~54% gap on 2026-10-05 | Close 56.48 → open 87.21, 14.9M vol | Repricing, still unstable |
| Volatility | ATR more than doubled | ATR 4.88 vs ~2.2 pre-gap | Halve position size |
| Resistance | Band + post-gap high | 71.13 (Boll UB), 72.44, then 87.21–90.75 | Breakout gate at 72.44 |
| Support | Demand zone | 64.8 / 63.8; gap fill toward 56.48 | Invalidation below 63.8 |
| Pattern | Bullish reversal candle 10-09 | Open=low 64.78, close 71.38 near high | Buyers defending low-64s |

**Bottom line:** Bullish bias above ~64 with extreme volatility. The clean trade is either a confirmed breakout over 72.44 or a controlled pullback into 64–66 — everything in between is noise at ATR ~5.

## Sentiment Report: PCVX (Vaxcyte, Inc.) — 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-09

### 1. Source-by-source breakdown

**Yahoo Finance news — unavailable.** The feed returned a placeholder: it only serves recent items, so this is a coverage gap, not an absence of news for PCVX. No institutional framing could be assessed.

**Reddit (r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, r/investing) — unavailable.** Same limitation: the search only serves recent items, so silence here is not evidence of no discussion.

**StockTwits — 28 messages (the only live source).** Labelled sentiment: 3 Bullish (11%) vs 6 Bearish (21%), with 19 unlabeled. Among labelled posts the ratio is 2:1 bearish. The dominant story is a violent event-driven round-trip: VAX-31 OPUS-1 Phase 3 topline data sent the stock up ~57% intraday on Monday, then it fell 9.7% to ~$66.70 on Tuesday ('the data was the event, and the event is over' — @KryptonResearch14, citing Reuters). Multiple posts confirm the spike to over $100 followed by a sharp retracement ('this was over 100 yesterday at one point', '40-50 after hours', 'watched it go from 50s to 108'). A successful short thesis is visible and celebrated ('smart peeps… shorted it yesterday in $80-$90').

Bearish posts are specific: 'NO insider buys in 5 years' (@Mark609, twice-labelled Bearish), 'Nice short', 'This nothing burger is going down', '-20 by eod'. Bullish posts are thinner but forward-looking: 'just wait for the share selling to be complete by tomorrow and we can rocket', 'wants to go back through 75$', 'buyout soon?', and a volume-spread note citing VAX-31 catalysts with support at $62 and resistance at $72. Unlabeled messages skew toward shock/confusion at the reversal ('damn! What happened', 'the whole market is bleeding').

### 2. Cross-source divergences and alignments

Only one source is live, so true cross-source divergence cannot be tested. Within StockTwits itself there is a clear split: event-chasers and dip-buyers vs. a larger, more emphatic bearish cohort that views the post-data pop as a liquidity event to short. The unlabeled majority mostly registers disbelief at the volatility rather than directional conviction.

### 3. Dominant narrative themes

- **Binary biotech event overhang:** OPUS-1/VAX-31 Phase 3 topline was the event; sentiment now grapples with the aftermath — classic 'sell the news' behavior.
- **Capital-raise fear:** a bullish post explicitly waits for 'share selling to be complete', and others note 'they needed money', suggesting the market expects or is digesting dilution.
- **Insider-inactivity criticism:** repeated 'no insider buys in 5 years' frames governance cynicism.
- **Elevated speculative interest:** 8.2x normal volume and 'buyout soon?' chatter show the name remains a high-attention trading vehicle despite the drawdown.

### 4. Catalysts and risks

- **Catalysts:** completion of any secondary/share-sale overhang (potential short-term relief), continued VAX-31 pivotal readouts, buyout speculation, technical support at ~$62 / resistance at ~$72.
- **Risks:** dilution from financing, post-event momentum unwind toward $50–60, absence of insider buying as a confidence signal, and broad-market weakness ('the whole market is bleeding').

### 5. Summary table

| Signal | Direction | Source | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post-Phase-3 reversal | Bearish | StockTwits | +57% intraday then -9.7% to $66.70; 'the event is over' |
| Labelled stance ratio | Bearish | StockTwits | 6 Bearish vs 3 Bullish of 9 labelled |
| Short-thesis celebration | Bearish | StockTwits | 'shorted in $80-$90', 'Nice short' |
| Dilution/selling overhang | Mixed | StockTwits | 'wait for share selling to complete' → bullish after, bearish now |
| No insider buys | Bearish | StockTwits | @Mark609, repeated |
| Buyout/dip-buy speculation | Mildly Bullish | StockTwits | 'buyout soon?', 'A buy at 50', support $62/resistance $72 |
| News coverage | N/A | Yahoo Finance | Source unavailable (recency limit) |
| Reddit discussion | N/A | Reddit | Source unavailable (recency limit) |

**Bottom line:** Mixed, leaning mildly bearish. Retail sentiment is dominated by a violent post-data unwind and active short interest, countered by a minority betting on relief once the share-sale overhang clears. Confidence is low: two of three sources returned placeholders and the StockTwits sample is small (28 messages, only 9 labelled). Treat this as a volatility-regime signal, not a directional call.

# PCVX (Vaxcyte, Inc.) — Fundamentals Report
Point-in-time: 2026-10-09. All figures are SEC EDGAR facts as filed on or before that date, USD millions unless noted.

## Vendor/data limitations (material)
- `get_fundamentals` returned no profile/valuation block: market cap, multiples, 52-week range, sector/industry and even company name are present-day values with no 2026-10-09 vintage, so they were withheld. No P/S, P/E, EV, or market-cap view is possible from this vendor.
- `get_insider_transactions` was withheld: trades are dated by event date with no filing date, so insider buying/selling known to the market on 2026-10-09 cannot be reconstructed.
- Income statement rows Revenue, Cost of Revenue and Gross Profit are "unavailable (not tagged by this filer)" for every period — consistent with a pre-commercial/clinical-stage issuer rather than a data outage.
- No 2025-Q4 column appears in the quarterly set; latest filed quarter is 2026-06-30.

## What the statements say

**Business model / stage.** The complete absence of tagged revenue across 2019–2026, paired with large and growing operating losses, says PCVX is an R&D-stage company funding operations entirely from capital markets and investment income. Every financing event shows up clearly in the cash flow statement: +374 (2020, IPO-era), +205–637 (2022–2023), +2,444 (9M 2024), and +602 (Q1 2026).

**Losses are widening fast.** Quarterly net loss: -141 (2025Q1), -167 (2025Q2), -213 (2025Q3), -321 (2026Q1), -284 (2026Q2). Operating loss tracks the same path: -181, -226, -242, -346, -303. Trailing four reported quarters (2025Q3 through 2026Q2) sum to roughly -1.1B net loss — the burn rate roughly doubled year over year (2026Q1 net loss -321 vs 2025Q1 -141). Diluted EPS: -2.30 (2026Q1), -1.97 (2026Q2). The modest Q2 improvement vs Q1 is the only deceleration in the series, but one quarter is not a trend.

**Cash burn.** Operating cash flow was -513 for 1H 2026 (-281 in Q1, ~-232 in Q2), versus -431 for all of 9M 2025 — i.e., 2026 is burning in two quarters what took three quarters in 2025. Annualized operating burn is now roughly -1.0B. Capex is trivial (~6 in 1H26); this is an opex burn, not a capex cycle.

**Balance sheet still funded, but shrinking between raises.** At 2026-06-30: total assets 3,138; current assets 1,553; cash and equivalents only 183; total liabilities 380 (current 271); stockholders' equity 2,758. The pattern is a sawtooth: equity raises spike assets (2,091 → 3,560 across 2024), then losses grind them down (3,560 → 3,003 through 2025), then another raise (+602 financing in Q1 2026) lifts them again to 3,348 before Q2 burn takes them to 3,138.

**Liquidity runway.** Cash on hand (183) covers less than one quarter at the current ~250/quarter operating burn — but current assets of 1,553 imply most liquidity sits in short-term investments. Against ~1.0B annualized burn, current assets fund roughly 1.5 years. That is adequate but not comfortable, and history says this management team raises early and large rather than waiting.

**Leverage.** Minimal. Liabilities are ~12% of assets and mostly current operating liabilities; there is no evidence of meaningful debt. Solvency risk is a funding/dilution question, not a default question.

## Actionable read-through for traders
- This is a binary-catalyst, cash-burn story: valuation will be driven by clinical/regulatory news (outside this dataset) and by the next raise, not by anything in the P&L.
- Dilution risk is the dominant fundamental factor. Five major financing events in six years, most recently ~602 in Q1 2026. With ~1.0B/yr burn and 1.55B current assets, another equity raise within 4–6 quarters is the base case even with no further loss acceleration. Expect a shelf/ATM if not already in place.
- Watch the cash-vs-investments split: cash of 183 vs current assets 1,553 means headline "cash" understates liquidity, but also means reported burn depends on portfolio yields; watch interest/other income lines in future 10-Qs.
- Improving item: Q2 2026 loss narrowed vs Q1 (-284 vs -321). If Q3 confirms deceleration, the runway narrative improves; if it re-accelerates past ~350/quarter, the next raise pulls forward.
- Not available: market cap, multiples, insider transactions, revenue. Any trade thesis from this dataset alone is a funding-runway thesis, not a valuation thesis.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case: PCVX (Vaxcyte, Inc.)

Let me open by addressing the elephant in the room directly: yes, the stock gapped ~54% and faded. The bears will call this a "sell the news" unwind. I call it a repricing that the market hasn't finished — and the data actually supports my read.

## 1. The event that caused the gap was real value creation, not hype

On 2026-10-05, PCVX gapped from 56.48 to an open of 87.21 on 14.9M shares — roughly 7–10x normal volume. That was the market digesting **positive VAX-31 OPUS-1 Phase 3 topline data**. This isn't a rumor or a promotional press release — it's pivotal-stage clinical success in the company's lead pneumococcal conjugate vaccine program. A successful Phase 3 readout permanently raises the probability-weighted value of the entire franchise. Stocks don't gap 54% on nothing, and they don't *stay* repriced upward on nothing either — PCVX closed the week at 71.38, still ~26% above the pre-event close. The market kept most of the repricing. That's the tell.

## 2. The technicals say the pullback already resolved upward

The bear narrative — "the event is over, momentum dead" — is contradicted by Friday's price action:

- **2026-10-09 was a textbook bullish reversal candle:** open 64.78 (the day's low), close 71.38 near the high of 72.44. Buyers stepped in at the low-64s and defended it hard.
- **Full bullish stack:** 71.38 > 10 EMA 64.43 > 50 SMA 59.94 > 200 SMA 55.73, with the 50 well above the 200 and rising.
- **Momentum re-expanding, not exhausting:** MACD 2.22 vs signal 0.89 with a fresh positive crossover; RSI at 64.88 — elevated but *below* the overbought line, having cooled from 76.6 and now turning back up. That's the signature of a second leg, not a top.
- The post-gap low of ~63.79 held across three sessions of consolidation on elevated volume. That's accumulation behavior — weak hands sold into the spike, stronger hands absorbed the supply between 64–67.

A close over 72.44 opens a direct retest of the 87–90 gap-day zone. The risk is defined and nearby (~63.8 invalidation); the upside target is 20%+ away. That's the asymmetry bulls want.

## 3. The balance sheet can fund the opportunity

Bears will hammer the ~$1.0B annualized burn and widening losses. Fair — but incomplete:

- **$1.55B in current assets** against ~$1.0B burn is roughly 1.5 years of runway — adequate to reach the *next* catalysts without a distressed raise.
- **Essentially zero debt.** Liabilities are ~12% of assets, all operating. This is a funding-cadence question, not a solvency question — and management has demonstrated five times over that it can raise capital efficiently, most recently +602 in Q1 2026 *before* the stock re-rated. Raising at $70–90 is far less dilutive than raising at $56.
- **Q2 losses actually narrowed** (-284 vs -321 in Q1). One quarter isn't a trend, but the burn trajectory is not accelerating out of control.

Here's the counterintuitive point the bears miss: the StockTwits chatter about "share selling completing" is *bullish*. If there's a financing overhang, it's transient — and once cleared, a $1.5B+ funded company with a de-risked Phase 3 asset is exactly the profile that trades up.

## 4. The strategic floor: this is a buyout-candidate asset

VAX-31 targets pneumococcal disease — a multi-billion-dollar market currently dominated by Pfizer's Prevnar and Merck's pneumococcal programs. A carrier-sparing, high-valency PCV with positive pivotal data doesn't just have standalone value; it's a strategic asset every large-cap vaccine and pharma player wants. The "buyout soon?" chatter on StockTwits isn't retail fantasy — it's the rational recognition that successful late-stage vaccine assets with clean balance sheets are prime M&A targets, and big pharma is chronically hungry for de-risked pipeline.

## 5. Refuting the bear's specific ammunition

- **"No insider buys in 5 years"** — insider buying at a funded clinical-stage biotech is a weak signal either way; insiders already hold equity-comp-heavy positions and companies at this stage don't signal via open-market purchases. The institutional re-rating on 14.9M shares is a far stronger vote.
- **"The event is over, sell the news"** — sell-the-news logic applies to approvals and launches where the catalyst is terminal. Positive Phase 3 data is an *enabling* catalyst: it unlocks filing, more readouts, and partnering. The catalyst runway has expanded, not ended.
- **"Shorts made money in $80–90"** — they did, and now they're covering into the 64–71 demand zone. Celebrated shorts at the top are fuel for the next leg, not a thesis against it.
- **Sentiment is 4.6/10 with low confidence** — in a post-event volatility regime, washed-out sentiment at a higher price base is historically where sustained moves start, not where they end.

## Bottom line

PCVX just delivered the single most important thing a clinical-stage biotech can deliver: positive pivotal data on its lead asset. The market re-priced it ~26% higher *net of the fade*, the chart resolved the post-gap consolidation upward with a picture-perfect reversal candle, the balance sheet funds ~1.5 years of runway with no leverage, and the asset sits in a category where big pharma pays premiums. The bears are fighting a Phase 3 success story with sentiment from short-sellers who already took their profit. I know which side of that trade I want.

**Bullish above ~64 with defined risk below 63.8; breakout confirmation over 72.44 targets 87–90.**

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case: PCVX (Vaxcyte, Inc.)

My bull colleague just spent five sections explaining why a stock that opened at 87.21 and closed the week at 71.38 is actually a win. Let me translate: the market was offered the chance to pay $87 for this asset on Monday morning, and by Friday it was paying $71. That's an ~18% decline *in four sessions* from the price the market itself chose in the immediate aftermath of the data. The bull calls that "kept most of the repricing." I call it what the tape calls it: distribution.

## 1. The gap-day candle is the most bearish artifact in this entire dataset

The bull keeps citing the "full bullish stack" of moving averages as if the MAs carry independent information. They don't — they're arithmetic echoes of a single 54% gap candle. Of course price is above the 10/50/200; the stock teleported. The *informative* price action is what happened after:

- **Open 87.21, high 90.75, close 73.82 on 14.9M shares.** The intraday fade from open to close was ~15%. That volume isn't a "vote" for the repricing — it's the largest single-day transfer of shares in the stock's history, executed at prices between 71 and 90 that the market has never revisited. Every one of those buyers above ~73.8 is underwater and will sell into strength. That's not a supply "shelf" — it's a ceiling of trapped longs with a defined exit price.
- The bull claims shorts "are covering into the 64–71 demand zone." Covering *at 64–71 after shorting at 80–90* is profit-taking on a winning trade — it confirms the direction of that trade was right. You don't get to cite short covering as bullish fuel while ignoring that the shorts were proven correct by 20+ points.

## 2. "Kept most of the repricing" is doing enormous work

Yes, +26% vs. pre-event close. But the correct benchmark isn't 56.48 — it's the price discovery that happened *after* the data was fully public. The market's verdict on fully-informed value was: spike to 90, settle at 64–67, dead-cat bounce Friday. The 2026-10-09 candle the bull loves (open = low, close near high) is real, but it happened on **4.4M shares** — roughly a third of the gap-day volume and a third of the mid-week consolidation volume (10.2M, 11.6M). A reversal candle on declining volume after a massive distribution event is a bounce, not an accumulation signature. The Friday close at 71.38 sits *exactly at* the upper Bollinger band and *exactly below* the 71.60 gap-day low / 72.44 resistance confluence. The bull's own framework says momentum entries belong above 72.44 — meaning at Friday's close, even the bull shouldn't be buying yet. The clean trades in their own report are "breakout over 72.44 or pullback to 64–66." Chasing at 71.4 is, by their own admission, "the worst reward-to-risk."

## 3. The fundamentals are worse than the bull frames

The bull waves at ~$1.0B annualized burn and calls the runway "adequate." Look at the actual trajectory:

- **Losses doubled YoY.** Net loss went -141 (2025Q1) → -321 (2026Q1). The Q2 "improvement" to -284 still leaves a trailing four-quarter burn of ~$1.1B and an *accelerating* operating cash drain: -513 in 1H 2026 vs. -431 in the first three quarters of 2025. The bull's claim that "the burn trajectory is not accelerating" is contradicted by his own data — 2026 burned in two quarters what took three quarters in 2025.
- **Actual cash is 183.** The 1.55B "current assets" is mostly short-term investments whose value fluctuates and whose existence the market is already discounting. Pure cash covers less than one quarter.
- **Five raises in six years, and the sixth is coming.** With ~$1.0B/yr burn, a raise inside 4–6 quarters is base case. Here's the part the bull glosses: the StockTwits chatter isn't about a *hypothetical* raise — posts say "they needed money" and bulls are literally waiting for "the share selling to be complete." A financing overhang may already be live *right now*. You don't get to call active dilution a bullish transient. And note the sequence the bull inadvertently highlighted: they raised $602M in Q1 2026 at ~$55/share, then announced Phase 3 data in October. Companies that are confident their data will re-rate the stock raise *after* the data. This one raised before.

## 4. "Phase 3 success permanently raises value" — does it?

The bull treats topline Phase 3 success as a terminal de-risking event. For a PCV program it is not:

- Topline ≠ approvable. Between here and a BLA filing sit the full dataset, consistency/lot data, FDA feedback, and a second pivotal (OPUS-2) — each a fresh binary. The history of pneumococcal vaccine development is littered with programs that looked great at topline and stumbled on serotype coverage, non-inferiority margins vs. Prevnar 20, or manufacturing comparability.
- **Competitive reality:** VAX-31 must displace entrenched, marketed incumbents (Pfizer's Prevnar franchise, Merck's VAXNEUVANCE) that already own contracting, ACIP relationships, and real-world safety data. Even a best-case approval lands PCVX in a share fight against the two best-capitalized vaccine franchises on earth — while PCVX is still pre-revenue and burning $1B/yr.
- The "buyout soon?" thesis the bull elevates is StockTwits speculation — the same source he dismisses when it posts "no insider buys in 5 years." You can't selectively quote retail chatter. And if big pharma wanted this asset, the rational move is to wait: every dilution makes the target cheaper, and the acquirer takes on the same competitive and regulatory risk either way.

## 5. The information environment is hollow
